issues.description: The problem statement's UML and requirements specify Stock.take(String) should return an int, but the template implementation of Stock.take(String) returns a boolean. The solution repository implements Stock.take(String) returning an int. This mismatch in the template will confuse students about the expected return type and semantics of take(), and will block following the problem's examples (which expect -1 on failure and a numeric remaining quantity on success).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template's Stock.take(String) signature and behavior to return an int like the UML and solution: return -1 if the ingredient does not exist or has insufficient quantity, otherwise decrement the quantity and return the remaining quantity. Update the method's return type from boolean to int and adjust its implementation accordingly so it matches the problem specification and the solution.

issues.description: The problem statement's class diagram specifies Stock.take(String): int (an int return used to signal remaining quantity or -1), and the solution implements Stock.take(String) returning an int. However, the template implementation of Stock.take(String) returns a boolean. This mismatch in the method's signature/return type for the same conceptual operation (taking one unit of an ingredient from stock) will confuse students: the problem and solution expect an int-based contract (e.g., checking for -1), but the template forces a boolean-based contract. It creates a breaking cognitive mapping and compilation friction when students implement SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() as described in the task.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template Stock.take(String) signature and behavior with the problem statement and solution: change the method to return int (return -1 when the ingredient is missing or insufficient, otherwise return the remaining quantity after taking one). Update the implementation accordingly so students can use the int return convention used in the diagram and solution.
